jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in CAR-T Cell Therapy  (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
The **Children’s Hospital Augsburg (Swabian Children’s Cancer Center) **and the University of Augsburg are looking for a Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in CAR-T Cell Therapy and Therapeutic Target Discovery in Pediatric and Rare Tumors to join our interdisciplinary research program at the interface of pediatric oncology, tumor biology, cellular therapy, therapeutic target discovery, and computational cancer biology. The position is a full-time position which is limited to two years.

The Children’s Hospital Augsburg (Swabian Children’s Cancer Center) is part of University Hospital Augsburg (UKA), a rapidly growing academic medical center with 1,699 patient beds across 22 clinics and approximately 2,800 employees. Scientifically, the hospital is a member of the NCT-WERA cooperation and thus one location of the National Center for Tumor Diseases (NCT).

**Research Environment **

- Single-cell, spatial, and multi-omic technologies are providing unprecedented opportunities to characterize tumor composition, heterogeneity, and evolution. Our research program combines these approaches with experimental tumor modeling to identify clinically actionable vulnerabilities in rare and high-risk tumors
- Our group has established a strong track record in the molecular characterization of pediatric and rare tumors, including rhabdoid tumors and other embryonal malignancies. Recent integrative studies have provided new insights into the biology and evolution of these tumors and opened avenues for therapeutic translation (Johann et al., Cancer Cell, 2016; Erkek, Johann et al., Cancer Cell, 2019; Fincke et al., Clinical Cancer Research, 2023; Mucha et al., Communications Medicine, 2025; Fincke et al., Nature Communications, 2026, accepted)
- A central goal of this position is the identification, prioritization, and experimental validation of therapeutic targets in rare entities for which effective treatment options remain limited. Relevant tumor types include DICER1-associated neoplasms, rhabdoid tumors, pediatric and rare melanomas, and other high-risk pediatric malignancies
- The successful candidate will combine molecular and computational analyses with state-of-the-art experimental approaches. CAR-T-cell therapy will represent a major experimental platform for evaluating candidate cell-surface targets and developing targeted cellular therapies
- Together with our partner institutions, we are establishing a growing biobank of patient-derived tumor organoids and other advanced tumor models, enabling systematic investigation of target expression, therapeutic efficacy, and mechanisms of resistance, including in vivo

**Your Responsibilities **

- Identify and prioritize novel therapeutic targets using integrated molecular, single-cell, spatial, and multi-omic data
- Experimentally validate candidate targets using patient-derived models, organoids, and cell lines
- Generate, engineer, and functionally characterize CAR-T cells
- Develop and optimize CAR constructs and cellular therapy strategies
- Evaluate CAR-T-cell efficacy and mechanisms of resistance in vitro and, ideally, in vivo
- Integrate experimental results with bioinformatic and computational analyses
- Develop independent research projects and contribute to grants and collaborative projects
- Publish and present research findings
- Mentor students and junior researchers where appropriate

Requirements

Mandatory

- PhD or equivalent degree in biology, molecular medicine, cancer biology, immunology, biotechnology, or a related field
- Hands-on experience in CAR-T-cell generation, engineering, and functional characterization
- Strong background in experimental cancer or cellular biology
- Experience in independent experimental research and data analysis
- Strong interest in therapeutic target discovery and translational cancer research
- Excellent communication and teamwork skills
- Excellent written and spoken English

Highly desirable

- Experience with therapeutic in vivo testing of CAR-T cells and/or xenograft models
- Experience with tumor organoids or patient-derived models
- Expertise in CAR design, viral transduction, T-cell expansion, flow cytometry, or functional immune-cell assays
- Experience in therapeutic target discovery and validation
- Familiarity with single-cell, spatial, or multi-omic approaches
- Programming skills in R or Python

What we offer

- Remuneration up to pay grade EG 13 TV-L, depending on qualifications and professional experience, including the standard social benefits provided in the public sector (occupational pension scheme and annual special payment)
- The position is initially limited to two years; an extension is intended, subject to funding and successful performance
- An interdisciplinary research environment combining experimental oncology, CAR-T-cell engineering, therapeutic target discovery, and computational cancer biology
- Integration into the research program of the University of Augsburg, with close collaboration with the University Hospital Augsburg and computational research groups
- The opportunity to work on rare and clinically challenging tumor entities, including DICER1-associated neoplasms, rhabdoid tumors, melanomas, and other high-risk pediatric malignancies
- Access to advanced patient-derived tumor models, including a growing collection of tumor organoids
- Opportunities to develop an independent academic profile, publish, present at international conferences, and contribute to grant applications
- International collaborations and opportunities for research visits with academic partner institutions

Contact

For further questions please refer to Prof. Dr. Pascal Johann (Pascal.Johann@uk-augsburg.de)

Application Deadline

Please submit your application as soon as possible, latest at the 15th of October 2026.

We look forward to you!

The position is suitable for people with severe disabilities. Applicants (m/f/d) with severe disabilities will be preferred if they are essentially the same aptitude, ability and professional performance. Women are invited to apply in accordance with Article 7 (3) BayGlG. When starting work at the Augsburg University Hospital, proof of sufficient immune protection in accordance with §§ 23, 23a IfSG must be presented or the same must be met.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come.

Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

At Roche, we believe precision medicine radically improves lives. Our Global CAP/CLIA laboratories are the "heartbeat" of diagnostic innovation, bridging the gap between early research and life-saving commercial diagnostics. As a Laboratory Manager, you aren't just overseeing a facility; you are leading a team that transforms complex biological data into the insights clinicians need to treat patients with cancer and other life-altering diseases.

We are seeking a high-caliber Laboratory Manager (m/f/d) to oversee our dual-specialty pathology and immunoassay laboratory. This role requires a unique blend of technical expertise in tissue-based diagnostics and immunoassay automated testing.

You will be responsible for the operational excellence of the lab, ensuring that both the Histology/Pathology and Immunoassay/Chemistry departments function at peak efficiency while maintaining total compliance with ISO15189, CAP (College of American Pathologists) and CLIA regulations.

The Opportunity

You will oversee a dual-specialty laboratory at the forefront of the industry. Your leadership will span two critical domains:
* Anatomic Pathology: Managing high-complexity tissue-based diagnostics, including advanced Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and In Situ Hybridization (ISH)
* Immunoassay Excellence: Driving peaks of operational efficiency in our automated immunoassay tracks on state-of-the-art cobas® platforms

You will also be a key driver in our Digital Pathology transformation, integrating whole-slide imaging and AI-based image analysis into routine clinical workflows to set new standards for diagnostic precision. Your key responsibilities:

* Visionary Operational Leadership: Supervise the daily "rhythm" of the lab, synchronizing pathology and immunoassay workflows to ensure competitive turnaround times (TAT)
* Guardian of Quality: Maintain an "inspection-ready" culture, serving as the primary lead for CAP/CLIA and ISO 15189 audits
* Champion of People: Lead, mentor, and inspire team of Laboratory scientists, fostering a culture of continuous learning and technical excellence
* Strategic Technical Oversight: Manage the validation and implementation of new assays and novel platforms, ensuring every piece of equipment is a high-performing component of our diagnostic system
* Innovate & Improve: Actively identify opportunities for workflow optimization and cost-effective management without ever compromising the quality that defines the Roche name

Who you are
* You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Clinical Laboratory Science, Medical Technology, or a related Biological Science. A Master’s (MHA/MBA) or PhD is highly preferred.
* Furthermore, you have 5+ years of experience in a clinical laboratory setting
* Proven expertise in both anatomic pathology and automated immunoassay workflows is a distinct advantage
* The ideal candidate isn't just a technical expert; You are a leader who fosters a culture of quality, safety, and continuous improvement with at least 2 years of experience in a leadership role
* You live the Roche mindset by maintaining a track record of zero-deficiency inspections and a passion for navigating the complexities of emerging global regulations

ALLEA e.V. is the European Federation of Academies of Sciences and Humanities, representing more 60 academies from 40 EU and non-EU countries. ALLEA operates at the interface of science, policy and society and acts on behalf of its members to promote science as a global public good, facilitate scientific collaboration across borders and disciplines, improve the conditions for research, provide the best independent and interdisciplinary science advice, and strengthen the role of science in society.  

For our Berlin office, we are seeking a versatile and committed

Communications Student Assistant

to join its team in Berlin as soon as possible for initially twelve months, with possibility of renewal, and with a weekly average workload of 19.5 hours. The hourly remuneration is in accordance with the Tarifvertrag für studentische Beschäftigte (TV Stud III), Berlin. 

Your role

You will work closely with other staff members to support the effective communication of our projects and activities, and to further strengthen the visibility of ALLEA in the scientific and policy community throughout Europe and beyond.  You will be supporting the day-to-day management of communications tasks within an international network.

Regular support of ALLEA’s communications activities:

- Support in establishing and maintaining media contact databases, creating stakeholder outreach lists, and designing strategies to communicate ALLEA’s work.
- Assist the communications team in drafting website posts and press releases, and in the day-to-day management of social media channels and blog
- Help prepare, edit, proofread, and layout ALLEA newsletters, publications, leaflets, etc.
- Support the team with preparation, execution, and follow-up of digital, hybrid or in-person public events as well as working group and committee meetings.
- Media monitoring, project administration and general office tasks are also part of this role.

What we are looking for:

- Be a graduate student enrolled in a university programme for at least 12 months after starting the ALLEA position, preferably in a communications-related field (communications or media studies, journalism, marketing, etc.), or in other social science fields (international relations, sociology, political science, etc.) with a strong interest in communications.
- Have an excellent command of English in speaking and writing; other language skills are an asset.
- Have advanced computer skills, particularly MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point), experience with MS Office 365 and/or Zoom are an asset.
- Ideally have experience with Canva, AI software, WordPress and Adobe InDesign (experience with Photoshop and Premiere are also valuable) or be very motivated to learn the technical aspects of these programmes.
- Have very good organisational skills, hands-on approach, and a keen eye for detail; ability to work independently and in a team; flexibility with regards to working in an office setting or remotely as needed.
- Have an interest in ALLEA’s areas of expertise (international relations, public policy, scientific collaboration, science communications, research policy, scientific advice to policymaking, etc.)

- Options to work flexibly between our office facilities in the centre of Berlin and remotely.
